name: Regular City Council Meeting - 6:00 p.m.
agenda_text:
City of Encinitas
Regular City Council Meeting - 6:00 p.m.
AGENDA
WEDNESDAY, MAY 8, 2019 -
06:00 PM
p.m.
City of Encinitas - City Council Chambers
505 S. Vulcan Avenue
Encinitas, California 92024
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
2.
ROLL CALL
3.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
4.
SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS AND PROCLAMATIONS
4A.
Presentation by NCTD Chief Operations Officer – Transit Planning & Bus Operations Damon Blythe and Director of Service Planning Kim Hayford
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a “WHITE” speaker slip to the City Clerk. If needed, Oral Communication items will be referred to the City Manager either for resolution by administrative action or placement on a future agenda.
6.
REPORT FROM CLOSED SESSION (IF HELD)
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a “PINK” speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
If a public hearing item is part of the consent calendar, the public hearing shall be deemed held if the item is not removed from the consent calendar for discussion and possible action.
8A.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants.
2019-05-08 Item 08A Warrants
8B.
Encinitas Habitat Stewardship Program Assessment Report to consider public open space habitat management priorities and costs associated with program implementation. Contact Person: Principal Planner Langager
Direct staff to implement the Encinitas Habitat Stewardship Program pursuant to the recommendations specified in the Site Assessment Report (Attachment 1 of the agenda report).
2019-05-08 Item 08B Habitat Stewardship Program
8C.
Appointments to the Youth Commission. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
The Mayor, with the approval of City Council, appoints eight (8) applicants to the Youth Commission with terms ending June 2020.
2019-05-08 Item 08C Appointments to the Youth Commission REDACTED
8D.
Capital Project and Grants Update - Capital Improvement Program and Traffic Engineering Divisions. Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
Receive the report on the status of Capital Improvement and Traffic Engineering projects and grants.
2019-05-08 Item 08D Capital Projects and Grants Update
8E.
Design Services Contract for the FY 2019-2020 Citywide Sewer Rehabilitation Project (CE04H and CC04E). Contact Person: Associate Civil Engineer Widelski
Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to execute a contract in consultation with the City Attorney, and any necessary amendments and time extensions with Dudek in the amount of $348,841 plus 15 percent contingencies to design the FY 2019-2020 Citywide Sewer Rehabilitation Project, for a total contract amount not to exceed $401,168.
2019-05-08 Item 08E Design Contract for FY2019-2020 Citywide Sewer Rehab
8F.
Standardize pavement marking symbol for pedestrian facilities. Contact Person: City Traffic Engineer Bandegan
Approve the standard pavement marking symbol (presented in the agenda report), as recommended by the Traffic and Public Safety Commission.
2019-05-08 Item 08F Standardize Pavement Marking Symbol for Pedestrian Facilities
8G.
Construction Contract for the Bonita Drive Sidewalk Improvements Project, (CS19C). Contact Person: Associate Civil Engineer Widelski
Authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to execute a contract in substantial form as attached and any necessary amendments and time extensions in consultation with the City Attorney, with Lightning Fence Company in the amount of $63,426 plus 15% contingency ($9,514) to construct the Bonita Drive Sidewalk Improvements Project, for a total contract not to exceed amount of $72,940.
2019-05-08 Item 08G Bonita Drive Construction
8H.
Extend temporary light use at Leo Mullen Sports Park for Encinitas Express. Contact Person: Recreation Services Manager Karlen
Authorize the City Manager to extend the compliance agreement between the City of Encinitas and Encinitas Express for temporary light use at Leo Mullen Sports Park for one year.
2019-05-08 Item 08H Extend temporary light use at Leo Mullen Sports Park for Encinitas Express
8I.
Legislative position letter in opposition to AB 1763 (Chiu). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in opposition of AB 1763 for the Mayor’s signature.
2019-05-08 Item 08I AB1763 Letter of Opposition
8J.
Ratify Amendment 7 and Authorize Design Services for the East Side “Temporary” Improvements for the North Coast Highway 101 Streetscape Project (CS04D). Contact Person: City Engineer Wimmer
1) Ratify Amendment 7 to the agreement with Michael Baker International (MBI) in the amount of $60,300 for CEQA analysis, design, and traffic engineering services approved by City Council on August 24, 2016 for a not-to-exceed total amount of $2,254,225; 2) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, in consultation with the City Attorney, to execute an amendment to the existing agreement with MBI in the amount of $335,500 for the design of temporary improvements on the east side of North Coast Highway 101 in Leucadia for a not-to-exceed total amount of $2,589,725 including Recommendation 1 above; and 3) Authorize a 10% contingency up to $39,580 for all work, for a grand total of $435,380 to complete the tasks above for a not-to-exceed total amount of $2,625,306 including Recommendations 1 and 2 above.
2019-05-08 Item 08J Streetscape Extra Work East Side Improvements
8K.
Legislative position letter in opposition to SB 50 (Weiner). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in substantial form as attached in opposition of SB 50 for the Mayor’s signature.
2019-05-08 Item 08K SB50 Letter of Opposition
8L.
Legislative position letter in opposition to SB 330 (Skinner). Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Piatt
Approve the position letter in opposition of SB 330 for the Mayor’s signature.
2019-05-08 Item 08L SB330 Letter of Opposition
8M.
Authorization to upgrade Microsoft email software. Contact Person: IT Operations Supervisor Contreras
1) Approve upgrading email to Microsoft Exchange Online for Government and authorize the implementation of Option 1, as shown in Attachment 1 (migrating email to a virtual hosted environment designed for government customers); and 2) Authorize Microsoft Exchange Online subscriptions in an amount of $37,080 in FY 2019-20; and authorize anticipated subscriptions in amounts of $46,000 in FY 2020-21 and$50,719 in FY 2021-22 using Microsoft 365 for U.S. Government pricing for a total of $133,799.
2019-05-08 Item 08M Microsoft Exchange Online
8N.
Amendment 13 to the Agreement with Tyler Technologies, Inc. for the purchase of Tyler 311 Incident Management for Communities for a total not to exceed of $1,244,875.30. Contact Person: IT Applications Supervisor VanPelt
Approve Amendment 13 in substantial form as attached, in consultation with the City Attorney. Authorize the City Manager to execute the amended agreement with Tyler Technologies, Inc., for Tyler 311 Incident Management for Communities in the amount of $10,500 and recurring annual software maintenance fees in the amount of $1,000 for a total contract amount not to exceed $1,244,875.30.
2019-05-08 Item 08N Tyler Contract Amendment 13
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
PROCEDURES FOR PUBLIC HEARINGS ON APPEALS (ITEMS 10A and 10B): New information such as documents, exhibits, letters, photos, charts, diagrams, videos, etc., WILL NOT be considered by the City Council if presented at this meeting. All material must have been submitted to the City Clerk no less than 7 calendar days prior to this hearing.
10A.
Public hearing to consider an appeal of the Planning Commission’s approval of a Variance request to reduce side yard setbacks for a new twinhome project. The appellant is specifically appealing condition SCA2 of the Planning Commission Resolution No. PC 2019-04 that requires an additional one-foot dedication of a sewer easement. CASE NUMBER: 14-287 V/DR/CDP; APPLICANT: Hosseini; APPELLANT: Hosseini; LOCATION: 2155 Manchester Avenue (APN: 261-062-07). Contact Person: Associate Planner Mierau
Deny the appeal and adopt Resolution No. 2019-31 affirming the decision of the Planning Commission to approve the project with condition SCA2.
2019-05-08 Item 10A Hosseini Appeal - Case #14-287VDRCDP
10B.
Public hearing to consider an appeal of the Development Services Director’s approval of a two-lot subdivision and associated site improvements for the property located at 2218 13th Street. CASE NUMBER: 17-206 TPM; APPLICANT: Lewis Bernard Massie; APPELLANT: Darren Kimble c/o The Law Office of Julie M. Hamilton; LOCATION: 2218 13th Street (APN: 264-143-41). Contact Person:
Deny the appeal and adopt Resolution No. 2019-04 affirming the decision of the Development Services Director to approve the project.
2019-05-08 Item 10B Massie Appeal - Case #17-206 TPM
11.
INFORMATIONAL ITEMS - NONE
12.
COUNCIL MEMBER INITIATED AGENDA ITEM - NONE
13.
CITY COUNCIL MEMBER REPORTS PURSUANT TO AB1234 (GC 53232.3(d)) / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF
14.
CITY MANAGER REPORTS / PENDING POSSIBLE FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
2019-05-08 Item 14 CITY MANAGER FOLLOW UP LOG

CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

ADJOURNMENT - THE NEXT REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING WILL BE HELD ON MAY 15, 2019
Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
